PhD Dissertation · 2020

Observations of Helical Plasma Dynamics Using Complementary X-Ray Diagnostics in the MST

Department of Physics, University of Wisconsin–Madison · Advisor: Daniel J. Den Hartog

Access Full Thesis (PDF) ↗ meSXR Python Code ↗

Overview

High-temperature magnetically confined fusion plasmas emit substantial soft and hard X-ray radiation. While this radiation represents an energy loss channel, a plasma’s X-ray emission spectrum encodes rich information about its electron temperature (Te), impurity composition (nZ and Zeff), fast non-thermal electron populations, and internal magnetic topology.

This dissertation details the calibration, installation, forward modeling, and Bayesian Integrated Data Analysis (IDA) of a novel Multi-Energy Soft X-Ray (ME-SXR) diagnostic based on the DECTRIS PILATUS3 100K hybrid photon-counting detector on the Madison Symmetric Torus (MST) reversed-field pinch (RFP). Together with a complementary suite of X-ray diagnostics—a two-color diode-based soft X-ray tomography array, the NICKAL2 Ross filter spectrometer, and a fast avalanche-photodiode hard X-ray (FXR) camera—this system was used to investigate the structure and evolution of self-organized quasi-single helicity (QSH) helical plasma equilibria.

Summary of Key Findings

1. Diagnostic Development & Bayesian Integrated Data Analysis

Per-Pixel Multi-Energy Calibration

Calibrated the ~100k-pixel PILATUS3 detector across low-energy (1.6–6 keV) and medium-energy (4–14 keV) ranges by scanning individual pixel trimbit thresholds against X-ray fluorescence targets. Demonstrated an effective threshold resolution of ΔE < 100 eV (σE = 300 eV) in high-gain mode and ΔE < 200 eV (σE = 550 eV) in medium-gain mode, and validated an analytical charge-sharing model across both regimes.

Collisional-Radiative Forward Model

Built a comprehensive Python forward model combining in-situ spatial calibration, filter and detector response functions, and ADAS collisional-radiative atomic physics. Demonstrated that charge-exchange with neutral hydrogen significantly shifts aluminum ionization balance (Al+11 and Al+12 line emission at ~2 keV) in MST plasmas, and validated the synthetic predictions against simultaneous SXR tomography measurements.

Simultaneous Profile Inference via IDA

Developed methods to identify mid-Z impurity emission lines (such as Ar+16 at 3.05 ± 0.02 keV) and integrated the ME-SXR forward model with Thomson scattering, SXR tomography, and Ross spectrometer data inside a Bayesian MCMC framework to simultaneously reconstruct self-consistent Te, impurity density (nAl, nC), and Zeff radial profiles.

2. Helical Plasma Dynamics & Enhanced Confinement (QSH)

First Time-Resolved 2D Helical Te Profiles

Produced the first time-resolved 2D electron temperature and density reconstructions in a helical MST plasma by combining SXR tomography and far-infrared (FIR) interferometry within a forward-modeling framework mapped onto 3D helical equilibria (SHEq). Observed peak temperatures Te > 700 eV and steep temperature gradients |∇Te| ≥ 3 keV m−1, providing direct evidence of an internal thermal transport barrier.

Discovery of the QSH “Quiet Flattop Phase”

Demonstrated that the saturated QSH flattop divides into two distinct regimes: an initial self-organized quiet phase where secondary tearing modes are nearly absent and a broad hot thermal structure forms, followed by a dynamic phase where low-amplitude secondary tearing resumes and the hot region contracts into a narrower helical core. Runaway electrons (Er ≈ 15–18 keV) are well-confined during the quiet phase and rapidly lost at the transition.

Predator-Prey Dynamics & High-Frequency Fluctuations

Observed a 180° out-of-phase predator-prey oscillation between the dominant n = 5 tearing mode and secondary (n = 6, 7, 8) modes, with the soft X-ray emissivity gradient oscillating in phase with the dominant mode—confirming predictions of shear-suppression transport barrier theory. Also identified localized 400–1000 kHz magnetic fluctuations aligned with the helical structure, suggestive of gradient-driven microtearing turbulence.
